subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After a configured maintenance timeout releases the session lane, should OpenClaw preserve same-session maintenance coalescing until the non-cooperative worker settles, or intentionally allow a replacement maintenance run to overlap it?
rationale: The queue can release a timed-out promise but cannot forcibly stop plugin-owned `maintain()` work; choosing between deferred retry, overlap, or an SDK cancellation contract sets the persistent session-state and plugin compatibility semantics.

options.title: Preserve coalescing after timeout
options.body: Keep a timeout-afterlife marker that lets foreground turns proceed while later maintenance triggers coalesce until the old worker settles, then schedule at most one follow-up run.

options.title: Permit overlapping retry
options.body: Release the lane and allow the next trigger to start a replacement maintenance worker even while the original worker remains alive, accepting plugin-lock and ordering risk.

options.title: Define cancellable maintenance
options.body: Add a separately designed context-engine cancellation contract before enabling retries, so timeout can request cooperative termination rather than leaving detached work alive.

recommendation.title: Preserve coalescing after timeout
recommendation.body: Keep a timeout-afterlife marker that lets foreground turns proceed while later maintenance triggers coalesce until the old worker settles, then schedule at most one follow-up run.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a core queue/session lifecycle and plugin-contract decision rather than a mechanical test or documentation change.
